Apple's proposed solution to the memory shortage (or at least one mitigation) is to source memory from two Chinese companies, CXMT and YMTC.

While not technically prohibited, this would put Apple in direct conflict with the US government — and the idea now looks even more unfeasible due to two new developments…

Back in June, we learned that Apple was seeking approval from the Trump administration to source memory chips from China. While there is no actual law preventing companies from doing so, a Pentagon blacklist means that using chips from these two companies could result in iPhones being banned from sale to some or all federal government employees. It would also expose the Cupertino company to significant political or public relations risks.

We said at the time that the chances of the iPhone maker getting approval seemed slim; now a new report has hammered another nail into the coffin of this plan.

First, although sourcing from these two Chinese companies is not currently illegal, a New York Times report suggests this may soon change.

Second, even if everything remains the same, a Wall Street Journal report indicates that CXMT simply cannot meet Apple's order requirements.

I previously described this as an unlikely plan; now I would say the idea is nothing short of a pipe dream.
